text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Moslem-Croat Federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic meets representatives of coal miners from central Bosnia and town of Tuzla. He says miners have right to strike but authorities will not tolerate blockages of road traffic.
- The Moslem chairman of the Bosnian collective Presidency Alija Izetbegovic sends Christmas greetings to all Bosnian citizens of the Orthodox Christian faith.

- United States Agency for International Development (USAID) gave 43 loans in total of 28 million German marks to Bosnian private and public companies in 1996, coordinator John Heard says in interview.
- Bosnian Minister of Foreign Affairs Jadranko Prlic says international donors pledged $2.7 billion in first year of peace process. Funds will be spent in the first half of 1997.

- Bosnian council of ministers will at its next session discuss disputed Bosnian town of Brcko and possible plans to resettle Serbs from Croatia's Eastern Slavonia enclave in Brcko, council co-chairman Haris Silajdzic says.

- Top priority for Bosnia at upcoming donors' conference in Brussels will be housing of refugees and displaced persons, newly-appointed Bosnian Minister for Economy and Foreign Trade Hasan Muratovic says.

- Esad Landzo, a indicted Moslem war criminal, planned to commit suicide with sedatives in The Hague prison of the U.N. war crimes tribunal but attempt was prevented at last moment, his lawyer Mustafa Brackovic says.

- German car producer Volksvagen will invest three million German marks for protection of remaining equipment in devastated Sarajevo Car Factory (TAS), its pre-war partner. But 70 million marks are needed for renewal of production, manager Husein Musabegovic says.
- Sarajevo commercial bank, "Central Banka", has signed general agreement with American Express and first credit cards are expected to be issued in March 1997, bank manager says.
